coherence.reasons: Both documents use the same three-part hierarchy (closing does not pay; closure breaks or cannot prove the constraints; optimize, test, gate) with the same executive summary and near-identical slide titles and supporting evidence. X splits the cross-dock evidence and the Reading A/B sensitivity into separate slides; Y merges them and puts the answer in the executive-summary title. Neither structure makes the logic more or less consistent. The garbled titles on Y's slides 9–10 and the missing numbers on X's slide 6 are extraction artefacts, not reasoning flaws.

judgment.reasons: The recommendations are identical: keep East in 2027, approve Option K, run a capped all-ZIP cross-dock test through holiday and spring peaks, and decide the 2029 lease at a Q3 2028 gate with four criteria; close-to-Central is dropped. Both weigh the same five options on the same five tests, both run the Reading A/B sensitivity on the $0.85M minimum, and both show the same break-even volumes and reversibility trade-off. Both match the key's preferred recommendation R1 and meet all its defensibility criteria. There is no meaningful difference in how alternatives or trade-offs are weighed.

evidence.reasons: Both get every required calculation right: $1.20M incremental cost, $0.10M net saving, 389.6k against 360k capacity, and a 90.3% network SLA. Both correct the 98% versus 96% claim, the confounded renewal claim and the limits of the six-week pilot, and both flag the same assumptions as illustrative. Y shows slightly more of the working: the full three-term SLA sum (168.0k + 150.4k + 133.0k) ÷ 500k, 451k delivered against 460k needed, the 200k × ($13 − $8) transport step, and a 2028 step in the waterfall that takes the saving to zero. X reaches the same figures with a little less visible derivation. The edge is marginal and neither makes an unsupported claim the other avoids.

revision.reasons: Both handle the CEO's hypothesis the same way, and in line with the key's keep-with-conditions expectation. Each tests it against five conditions (holds, partly, partly, holds, holds) and refines it three ways: optimize rather than merely retain; capacity rules out only close-to-Central, not the cross-dock; and keep East through 2029, not permanently, with a gate. Both also note that the corrections cut against the inflated pro-East claims (98% and the renewal claim) as well as the CFO's saving.

overall.reasons: The two documents are substantively the same analysis with the same numbers, recommendation, gate criteria, sensitivities and risk handling. Y shows slightly more explicit arithmetic and a longer list of follow-up actions; X assigns owners to next steps and gives the cross-dock evidence and the minimum-fee sensitivity their own slides. These differences are negligible for the decision maker; either document would serve the board equally well.
